You’re one of the 16 actors in the MFA in Acting at the David Geffen School of Drama at Yale University, chosen from this year’s auditions with the 15 others you’ll be cast beside and against. Tuition is covered, as it is for every student. The fall term begins with registration, then orientation until August 29, 2026, and classes start on August 31, 2026, at 9 a.m.
Fall Term 2026 Begins

Tuition, $20,375.00 a term, is covered by the tuition scholarship. Yale’s aid for living costs goes by need, and your family’s means rule it out, so this term’s Yale Health plan, $1,882.00, was paid from your bank, and living costs are yours.
Registration And Your Account

Your tuition, $20,375.00 a term, is covered by the tuition scholarship. The aid office found no financial need, so you pay the Yale Health plan, $1,882.00 a term, yourself. Work-study is 150 assigned hours a year at $23.00 an hour: a shift each Saturday while classes run.
Meeting Your Class
You met the 15 others in your class: you’ll partner them in scenes, rehearse with them and be cast beside them.
Meeting The Acting Faculty

You met the acting faculty, with the chair, Tamilla Woodard. First-year courses are taught by Gregory Wallace, Walton Wilson, Julie Foh, Erica Fae, Fabio Tavares, Justine Williams, Tamilla Woodard, Kelsey Rainwater, Michael Rossmy and Paul Walsh. They set out what the School asks: attendance at every class, rehearsal and call; telling your teachers and the chair when you’re ill; Pass/Fail courses, and an Incomplete made up within a month; the casting pool, the Cabaret and work-study. It’s all kept on the Standing tab.
